AcceptanceView.description:
One acceptance condition — what must be measurably true for the task to count as done.

The same shape is both the **input** (`task/create`) and the **view** (what is required), so the card can never show a condition the verifier does not check.

argv.description: `commandSucceeds`: the program and its arguments. Never a shell string.

cwd.description: `commandSucceeds`: working directory, relative to the task's directory. Absent = the root.

expectedJson.description: JSON-encoded expected value. A string preserves the difference between absent and JSON null.

label.description: The human's own wording, when they gave one. Absent = derived from the fields above.

path.description: Path, relative to the task's working directory (an absolute path must land inside it).

pattern.description: Plain substring for `fileContains` — **not** a regex: a badly written pattern must not be able to stall a whole round.

pointer.description: RFC6901 pointer for jsonEquals; empty selects the complete document.

refPrefix.description: `receiptConfirmed`: a receipt whose ref starts with this, in status `confirmed`, must exist.

AgentTaskView.description: One task as the human sees it. `status` is a string on the wire (pending / running / suspended / needsAttention / done / failed / cancelled) — the dashboard paints it.

acceptance.description: What must be measurably true. An empty list provides no independent acceptance evidence.

checks.description: The latest verdict per condition, same order as `acceptance`.

currentTurnId.description: The turn currently carrying this task (a heartbeat; absent when idle).

cwd.description: The task's own working directory (the boundary for verification and writes).

dispatchState.description: pending / claimed / finished / interrupted; absent for conversational tasks.

executionSessionId.description: Separate task transcript, when explicitly started through task/start.

goalCondition.description: Optional condition evaluated by the goal judge. Acceptance checks can also trigger additional rounds.

inputCondition.description: Human-declared input obligation; it never grants tool permissions.

lastStopReason.description: Why it stopped last time — the card's footnote, never guessed from the status.

parentTaskId.description: The human-selected parent coding task whose worktree receives this child's checkpoint.

runCount.description: How many times this task has been executed ("run 3 times").

sessionId.description: Absent = a task that belongs to no conversation.

source.description: Where the task was dispatched from (a chat group); absent = a local view.

tier.description: The declared model tier (`fast` / `chat` / `reasoning`); absent = per-turn decision.

worktreePath.description: Set when `cwd` is a Jeeves-made git worktree: its path and branch. Never auto-deleted.

ApprovalLogEntry.description: One row of `approval/log`: the complete record of one "ask before running".

actor.description: Who answered: `owner`, or the channel identity that clicked (`lark:<open_id>`). Empty for a timeout or a voided request, and for rows written before this was recorded.

outcome.description: One of approved / denied / timeout / voided.

ApprovalLogEntry.title: ApprovalLogEntry

entries.description: Newest first, capped at 100 entries by the server.

ApprovalPendingParams.description: Live requests belonging to a conversation, including its task executions.
ApprovalPendingParams.title: ApprovalPendingParams

ApprovalRequestedNotification.description:
A "may I execute this?" query.

After throwing the question to the client the server **waits** (120 s by default); the answer arrives via `approval/respond`. No reply, timeout, or no approval channel at all — everything is **treated as denied**: default-deny is this feature's foundation, not its edge case.

argsPreview.description: Human-facing action preview: the raw command or an args summary.

expiresInMs.description: How many milliseconds of silence count as a denial.

reason.description: Why the allow rules did not let it through automatically.

requestId.description: Request id within this turn; echo it back verbatim when answering.

tool.description: What wants to run (tool name; currently only `run_command`).

version.description: Starts at 1 and rises each time the question is re-issued (a restart). Echo it in `approval/respond`; an answer carrying an older version is refused.

actor.description: Who answered, for the audit record: `lark:<open_id>` for a group dispatcher's card click, absent for the Runtime's owner. Recorded, never trusted for permission — the gateway already checked the clicker against the dispatcher list.

remember.description:
How long the yes lasts: `once`, `session` (memory only), `always` (settings.json).

**Required**, deliberately: no implicit default, so a client cannot forget to say how long a yes lasts and get `once` by accident. (It also keeps the generated Python model honest — an enum default comes out of `datamodel-codegen` as a bare string, a type error the SDK would then have to live with.)

What gets remembered is decided by the asking tool and named on the card: for `run_command` it is the command itself (no wildcards — the human approved this line, not this kind), for `write_file`/`edit` it is the **directory** (never the file name). A remembered rule still meets hard-deny, the sandbox and the writable boundary.

version.description: The `version` of the question being answered. Absent = the client does not track versions; present and stale = refused with a text error.

accepted.description: Is this request still awaiting an answer? False when the reply arrives too late (timed out, or the turn already ended) — the client learns nobody heard its answer.

answeredBy.description: When `accepted` is false because someone else answered first: who (`<channel>:<id>`), so a second channel can say "already answered by …". Absent when nobody answered (expired, or the question is unknown).

writtenText.description: Complete text of an observed successful whole-file write up to 64 KiB.

BrowserWorkerInfo.description: Every worker response carries a compatible handshake and process identity.

BudgetView.description: A task's budget. An absent field means that dimension is uncapped.

CalendarConnectorSettings.description: Human-only configuration. These fields contain references to credentials, never their values.
CalendarConnectorSettings.title: CalendarConnectorSettings

CapabilityCard.description: One capability and its state. Never carries a secret: `secretPointer` says where a key lives (`env:NAME` / `keychain` / `file`), not what it is.

identity.description: Who it acts as (an app id, a profile's provider), when known.

lastCheckedAt.description: Unix seconds of the last probe.

CapabilityCard.title: CapabilityCard

CapabilityKind.description: What kind of thing a capability card describes.
CapabilityKind.title: CapabilityKind

CapabilityState.description: Whether a capability can be used right now, and if not, why.
CapabilityState.title: CapabilityState

CheckView.description: One condition's latest measured verdict. Same order as `AgentTaskView.acceptance`.

artifactSha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact file bytes read for this measurement, when applicable.

detail.description: Passed: the evidence ("report.md 12.4 KB"). Failed: the measurement ("report.md does not exist").

label.description: The condition in the human's words ("report.md contains at least 3 conclusions").

argv.description: The program and its arguments. Never a shell string.

keys.description: Fetch only these keys; absent = return everything.

config.description: The full config after writing, so the frontend can replace its local cache outright.

ConnectorOAuthStartResponse.description: A prepared authorization URL. Its loopback callback is on the Runtime host.
ConnectorOAuthStartResponse.title: ConnectorOAuthStartResponse

ConnectorSettingsSaveParams.description: Exactly one section is provided; the other and Feishu configuration stay unchanged.
ConnectorSettingsSaveParams.title: ConnectorSettingsSaveParams

ConnectorStatus.description: One configured connector, as far as the dashboard needs to know: which one, whether it can actually send, and how wide the door is (allowlist size).

allowRecipients.description: How many entries the recipient allowlist has. `0` means nobody — said, not implied.

newFacts.description: How many new facts this batch distilled; 0 means not due yet or nothing surfaced.

ContextPart.description: One section of the context: soul, memory, skills, tools, history, summary.
ContextPart.title: ContextPart

ContextUsage.description: How the window is spent this turn. `ratio` is `used / budget`, already computed: the frontend must not have to guess which denominator was meant.

notice.description: Set once `ratio` crosses `JEEVES_CONTEXT_WARN_RATIO`: one honest sentence, no dialog.

ContextUsage.title: ContextUsage

usage.description: `None` = no turn has run in this session yet.

DashboardData.description:
Everything the dashboard's first screen needs, fetched in one shot.

It is not the response to any RPC but the payload of the `jeeves dashboard` HTTP endpoint (`GET /api/data`). **Why it lives in the protocol crate**: the only criterion is that it crosses languages. The browser side type-checks against it, and hand-copying it would drift again — exactly what this whole effort exists to eliminate.

Fields reuse protocol types directly: the dashboard does no second modeling — it is just a view over these data.

connectors.description: Connectors configured on this machine (0.12.0). Read from connectors.json by ops: it is the same file the app-server registered tools from, on the same machine.

connectorsError.description: Why the connector file could not be read, if it could not — the panel shows this instead of silently pretending there are no connectors.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601, millisecond precision. The page shows "when is this data from".

task.description: The viewed session's current task (goal upgraded to a persisted entity), when asked for.

taskArtifacts.description: What that task actually produced: files that exist, with their sizes (0.14). Always present (empty when there is no task), so the card needs no branch to render it.

todos.description: The viewed session's todo sheet, when asked for and non-empty. This is the model's own working sheet (todo_write), shown to the human as the task card.

DashboardData.title: DashboardData

kind.description: What this fact is **about**: `user` / `feedback` / `project` / `reference` / `fact` (fallback). Anything that resists classification lands on `fact`.

FeishuWeeklyReport.description: Deliver a verified research digest to this allowlisted Feishu recipient.
FeishuWeeklyReport.title: FeishuWeeklyReport

GoalRoundNotification.description: One notification per goal-loop verdict — "why did it run another round" is never guessed.

reason.description: The judge's reason (or the reason for exiting).

GoalRoundNotification.title: GoalRoundNotification

InteractionSource.description: Where a dispatched message came from, kept on every task it creates so the report can go back to the same place.

senderId.description: The sender's id on that channel (a Feishu `open_id`).

InteractionSource.title: InteractionSource

InteractionStartParams.description: A human message in the long-lived entry point. There is no model-callable route.

messageId.description: Stable across retries of the same message; reuse with changed input is rejected.

source.description: Where the message came from when it is not a local view (a chat group). Absent = the owner at one of the Runtime's own views. A source whose sender is not in `JEEVES_DISPATCHERS` gets an ordinary conversation without the `task` tool.

InteractionStartParams.title: InteractionStartParams

id.description: null when the id cannot be parsed (e.g. the request itself is bad JSON).

JsonRpcMessage.description: Any frame the server sends back: a response or an error.
JsonRpcMessage.title: JsonRpcMessage

JsonRpcNotification.description: Server-initiated push (on SSE / stdio this is simply frame after frame of events).
JsonRpcNotification.title: JsonRpcNotification

result.description: The concrete shape depends on method; decoders narrow it to the matching `*Response` type themselves.

LedgerEntryView.description: One ledger row as the dashboard shows it: kind, a short preview, and whether the full bytes still exist (`exact`) or only a folded summary came through the backfill.

fidelity.description: `exact` | `folded` — a folded entry is honest about being a summary.

preview.description: First line(s) of the payload, already trimmed for a list row.

LedgerEntryView.title: LedgerEntryView

LedgerTurnView.description: One turn in the ledger list: what happened, and how much of it is still recoverable.

fidelity.description: `exact` when every row is exact; `folded` when the backfill touched it.

preview.description: One line: the user's first sentence.

LedgerTurnView.title: LedgerTurnView

removed.description: How many were actually deleted. 0 means there was no memory of this subject to begin with.

catalog.description: The generated catalog, byte-for-byte the text the prompt carries.

turnId.description: Present = also return this turn's entries.

MemoryListEpisodesResponse.description: The episode list. **No cursor**: `Episodes::recent` only fetches the most recent N by time desc — storage has no notion of offset. Rather than invent an unusable cursor, it honestly returns null.
MemoryListEpisodesResponse.title: MemoryListEpisodesResponse

MemoryObservation.description: References describe extraction context, not independent evidence of truth.

assessmentJson.description: JSON assessment for a source-bound temporary claim. Confidence is model-reported, not calibrated or independent verification; includes quotation and source-time expiry.

MemoryObservation.title: MemoryObservation

page.description: `None` = no such page (the dashboard shows the path and says so, not an empty page).

MemoryPageSummary.description: One row of the catalog (`index.md`): enough to choose a page, not enough to replace it.
MemoryPageSummary.title: MemoryPageSummary

sources.description: Provenance: the ledger rows this page was distilled from (`ledger:12345`).

validityOrigin.description: `human` or `consolidation`; absent for an unbounded legacy claim.

source.description: Defaults to `user` (said directly by the user). Consolidation passes `consolidation` when distilling from conversations, so the frontend can tell "you told it" from "it summarized itself".

fact.description: The full fact as written, with id — the frontend can insert it directly, no re-query needed.

MemoryValidityParams.description: Human-only replacement of a fact's validity window. Null removes a bound.
MemoryValidityParams.title: MemoryValidityParams

Message.description:
One message in session history: a row of `chat_log`.

Same conversation, second viewpoint alongside the live stream (`turnStarted` / `textDelta` / `turnCompleted`): the live stream lives only for **this connection** (gone on refresh); this one makes "refresh, switch devices, look back later" possible.

id.description: The chat_log row number. **Also the cursor**: it is `session/messages`' cursor. Row numbers over timestamps: both rows of one turn are written in the same second, so timestamps cannot order them.

meta.description: This turn's telemetry (gate / tools / iterations / model / usage), **present only on assistant rows**.

receiptStatus.description: Outcome of the run that issued this receipt, even after the task runs again.

taskId.description: Original task for a decision or completion notice in its owner's chat.

Message.title: Message

MessageRole.description:
A message's role. A **closed set** — deliberately no "unknown" escape hatch.

If some future `chat_log` really does grow other roles, `session/messages` will **skip** those rows rather than force a value in — so the frontend `switch` can stay exhaustive and "there is a third role to render" shows up at compile time.
MessageRole.title: MessageRole

ModelCapabilities.description: Explicit declarations for the profile's main model; absent fields retain defaults.

reasoningEffort.description: Responses only. Supported efforts depend on the selected model.

ModelProfileView.description: A profile's **view**: unlike the stored copy it contains no secret, only where the secret lives.

active.description: Whether this profile is currently active.

keySource.description: Where the credential lives: `keychain` / `file` / `env:VAR` / `memory` / none (local model). **A pointer, not the key itself** — the UI uses it to honestly show "where your key is stored".

vision.description: Whether this profile's model accepts images. `null` = follow the vendor's default model (the catalog row).

ModelProfilesParams.description: Response to `model/profiles`: all configured model profiles + the active one.
ModelProfilesParams.title: ModelProfilesParams

activeId.description: The currently active id (null when nothing is configured).
When the active profile is removed, active is cleared along with it.

ModelRoutesResponse.description: `model/routes`: the routing table as the panel shows it. Always three rows (the tiers are fixed), each maybe pointing at nothing — an empty table is a valid, honest state.

mode.description: `fixed` (default, active profile wins) or `auto` (per-turn tier pick).

ModelRoutesResponse.title: ModelRoutesResponse

ModelRoutesSaveParams.description: `model/routes/save`: write the whole table (no patch semantics — three rows are cheap and "replace the table" cannot leave a half-edited state behind).
ModelRoutesSaveParams.title: ModelRoutesSaveParams

ModelSaveParams.description: Parameters for `model/save`. `provider` is required only when **creating** — passing only `id` + `make_active` means switch.

apiKey.description: The key itself. Absent = keep as-is (changing models or switching never requires re-sending).

keyEnv.description: Use a key from an environment variable (pass a name like `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`): Jeeves only reads it and never copies it into any file.

makeActive.description: Make it active right after saving (default true — the smoothest on first setup).

vision.description: Whether this model accepts images. Absent = keep the vendor's default (patch semantics, same as `model`); `true` is how "this vendor's default is text-only, but *this* model sees" gets declared at the moment the profile is created.

ModelSaveParams.title: ModelSaveParams

active.description: Whether this profile is currently active.

current.description: The current model after switching (`provider / model`); null when not fully configured.

keyStoredIn.description: Where the credential **actually** landed: `keychain` / `file` / `env:VAR` / `memory` / `none`. Fall back to a plaintext file and say so honestly — never let the user assume the keychain.

request.description: expiresInMs is remaining time at snapshot, not a renewed approval deadline.

restored.description: True when this question outlived a restart: answering it grants the resumed turn a one-time yes for the same action instead of unblocking a live call.

PermissionMode.description: Human-selected policy, always bounded by enabled tools and their hard constraints.
PermissionMode.title: PermissionMode

RememberScope.description:
How long an approval answer lasts.

The distinction exists because "yes" is three different promises: *this time*, *until the process exits*, and *until revoked*. Conflating them either nags the human on every call or silently writes a standing rule they did not ask for.

oneOf.description: Just this once (the default): the next identical action asks again.
Until this process exits: kept in memory, never written to disk.

RememberScope.title: RememberScope

RequestId.description:
Request id: JSON-RPC allows a number or a string.

The number arm is `i32`, not `u64`: ts-rs maps `u64` to TypeScript `bigint`, while `JSON.parse` yields `number` — the client receives `1` typed as `bigint`: the kind of bug that never errors but only fails at runtime. Only `i32` crosses language boundaries — the same rule as v2.rs.
RequestId.title: RequestId

ResponsibilityContract.description: A recurring duty registered by a human. Sources identify evidence, never tool grants.

budget.description: A task's budget. An absent field means that dimension is uncapped.

ResponsibilityContract.title: ResponsibilityContract

RetryNotification.description:
A "retrying now" notice.

Retries are **never silent**: the user sees this message, not an inexplicable long pause.
RetryNotification.title: RetryNotification

RunResponse.description:
The task API's one-shot shape (`POST /api/run`): a whole turn in, one answer out.

Same request body as `turn/start` (`TurnStartParams`), no stream — the HTTP call returns when the turn finishes. Built for programs (CI, cron, another agent), not for a browser: the dashboard keeps SSE, because a person wants to watch the answer arrive.

model.description: The model that actually answered — the visible proof that a tier pin took effect.

routeReason.description: Why this model was chosen (`tier:fast → mini`, `auto:reasoning → ds-r1`); absent = no routing.

RunResponse.title: RunResponse

RunView.description: One execution of a task. A task may run several times; each attempt is its own account.

status.description: running / waiting / suspended / completed / failed / cancelled.

RunView.title: RunView

ScheduleChangeResponse.description: What `schedule/save` and `schedule/remove` answer: one sentence for the panel or the model.
ScheduleChangeResponse.title: ScheduleChangeResponse

ScheduleJob.description: One scheduled job as the capability center shows it: the declaration plus the runtime state.

catchUp.description: true = at-least-once (re-run once after a miss), false = at-most-once (give up).

claimedMinute.description: Non-null = the last run was interrupted; it is never replayed, a human acknowledges it.

lastFiredMinute.description: The last settled trigger minute (the dedup anchor); null if it never ran.

nextRun.description: The next fire, or null when the pattern can never match.

nextRunNote.description: Why `next_run` is null, when it is null for an interesting reason.

skill.description: The skill this job comes from, when `source == "skill"`.

source.description: `store` (saved in state.db, editable) or `skill` (a SKILL.md `schedule:` line, read-only here).

ScheduleJob.title: ScheduleJob

error.description: Why part of the answer is missing (a state read failed), so "never ran" and "cannot tell" differ.

jobs.description: All jobs sorted by name; an empty array when none was ever declared.

ServerNotification.description:
The full stream of events for one turn.

`type` is the discriminant — the frontend switches on it, Python uses a pydantic discriminated union. **No failure here should crash the client**: this only describes "what happened".

mode.description: Null preserves pre-existing runtime rules until a human selects a preset.

delta.description: A streaming text delta. Present only when `turn/start` passed `stream: true`.

oneOf.description: Retrying now (rate limit / transient fault): **sent every time**, never silent.
A command is waiting for approval: answer it first, then the turn continues.

argsPreview.description: Human-facing action preview: the raw command or an args summary.

expiresInMs.description: How many milliseconds of silence count as a denial.

reason.description: Why the allow rules did not let it through automatically.

requestId.description: Request id within this turn; echo it back verbatim when answering.

tool.description: What wants to run (tool name; currently only `run_command`).

version.description: Starts at 1 and rises each time the question is re-issued (a restart). Echo it in `approval/respond`; an answer carrying an older version is refused.

oneOf.description: One notification per goal-loop verdict — "why did it run another round" is never guessed.

reason.description: The judge's reason (or the reason for exiting).

args.description: The model-supplied arguments; structure depends on the tool.

toolUseId.description: The id the model minted for this call — the same id its result comes back under. Clients key on it: several read-only calls can be in flight at once.

oneOf.description: A chunk of live output from a running tool. Progress, not a result.

chunk.description: A chunk of output, as it arrived. Chunk boundaries are not meaningful.

output.description: The text the tool returned to the model. Failure details live here too — the turn is not aborted.

toolUseId.description: Same id as the matching `toolStarted`, so a client can settle the right row.

newFacts.description: How many new facts this batch distilled; 0 means not due yet or nothing surfaced.

oneOf.description: A checkpoint is being resumed after crash recovery (finished tools are not re-run).

iterations.description: How many loop iterations are already done (a checkpoint lands at each tool-results boundary).

oneOf.description: Someone added a sentence to a turn that was already running (0.16).

A checkpoint is being resumed: startup reconciliation found it unfinished and the loop continues from where it stood (finished tools are not re-run). The human said earlier "keep going until X" by starting the turn — resuming is not the model assigning itself work.

fromIterations.description: How many iterations the checkpoint had already completed.

reason.description: Why it is resuming (`reconcile: crash recovery`, …).

oneOf.description: A checkpoint is abandoned: the human interrupted the turn (or the session moved on) — it will NOT be auto-resumed. Suspended, not silently lost: the ledger says so.

reason.description: Why it was abandoned (`interrupted by user`, …).

oneOf.description: The task behind this turn changed state (created / running / suspended / done…).

sessionId.description: Absent for a task that belongs to no session.

oneOf.description: Boxed: its `TurnMeta` is an order of magnitude bigger than the others, and notifications are built per event and shipped via channels. ts-rs is transparent to `Box<T>`.

ServerNotification.title: ServerNotification

SessionCapabilitiesParams.description: One shell's declaration at connection time. `platform` / `transport` are labels for diagnostics, not a permission boundary: the engine never branches on them.

features.description: Capability names this shell can render or supply, e.g. "streaming", "images", "approval", "attachments". Unknown names are refused, not silently ignored.

transport.description: How this shell reaches the engine: "http-sse", "tauri-ipc", "ffi", "stdio".

SessionCapabilitiesParams.title: SessionCapabilitiesParams

SessionCapabilitiesResponse.description: The engine's answer. `accepted` / `unsupported` partition `features`; a newer client talking to an older engine sees the gap instead of guessing.

protocolVersion.description: Bumped only on a breaking change to the wire contract.

SessionCapabilitiesResponse.title: SessionCapabilitiesResponse

focus.description: What to keep in the summary ("the migration plan"), optional.

coveredTurns.description: How many turns the new summary covers.

SessionGetParams.description: Read one session's record. Same shape as a list entry — one type, no second modeling.
SessionGetParams.title: SessionGetParams

SessionMessagesParams.description:
Read what was said in a session.

**Why it exists**: without it, the conversation on the page lives only in the browser — a refresh erases it. Also the prerequisite for "switch session".

cursor.description: Fetch only messages **older** than this one (paging back through history). Absent = the newest page.

SessionMessagesParams.title: SessionMessagesParams

SessionMessagesResponse.description: Messages with the **newest first** — opposite to the conversation's direction, because "paging back" is the point: take the latest page, then follow `nextCursor` into the past.

activeInputs.description: User inputs of the current task turn, before it enters settled history. Newest page only.

nextCursor.description: Present only when older messages exist: pass it as the next cursor. null = the end.

SessionMessagesResponse.title: SessionMessagesResponse

mode.description: Null preserves pre-existing runtime rules until a human selects a preset.

confirmFullAccess.description: Explicit human acknowledgement is mandatory when entering full access.

cwd.description: The session's working directory: the **root of everything it may write** (tools refuse writes outside it). Absent = not chosen; the dashboard shows "choose a working directory".

forkedFrom.description: The session this one was forked from. Display only: the two are independent — deleting one must not affect the other.

title.description: The name a human gave it (migration 0018); when there is none, the first user message.

SessionUpdateParams.description:
Rename a session or rebind its working directory.

**`null`/absent = leave alone; `""` = clear.** Two different intents must not collapse into one: "I renamed it" and "I never touched the title" are different writes.

cwd.description: Must be an existing absolute path when non-empty (same admission rule as `turn/start`).

SessionUpdateParams.title: SessionUpdateParams

SessionViewParams.description: Which session to look at — the shared params of the dashboard's per-session reads (`todo/view`, `session/get`). One field, one shape, no per-method re-modeling.
SessionViewParams.title: SessionViewParams

SettingsPatch.description: The **write patch** for config. Pass only the fields to change; null means leave as-is.

execAllow.description: Whole-table replacement of the allowlist (`JEEVES_EXEC_ALLOW`) — what "remember this command" writes.

execEnabled.description: The three capability switches (`JEEVES_EXEC` / `JEEVES_WRITE` / `JEEVES_DELEGATE`). A saved value overrides the environment, and takes effect on the next turn without a restart.

writeAllowDirs.description: Whole-table replacement of the directories "remember this" accepted for **writes** (`write_file`/`edit` no longer ask inside them). Remembering a directory never widens the writable boundary — the containment check still runs first.

SettingsPatch.title: SettingsPatch

SettingsView.description: The **read view** of config. Fields are deliberately complete and non-optional: reading it yields the full current state.

historyTurns.description: Working-memory sliding window: only the last N turns go into the prompt.

SettingsView.title: SettingsView

SkillStat.description: One skill's turn count: how often its body actually entered a prompt.
SkillStat.title: SkillStat

SpentView.description: What the task has consumed so far. Always present (zeroes when nothing ran yet).

TaskActionParams.description: `task/suspend|resume|cancel`: address one task and say why (the reason is shown, not dropped).
TaskActionParams.title: TaskActionParams

TaskArtifactsResponse.description: `task/artifacts`: what this task actually produced, newest first.
TaskArtifactsResponse.title: TaskArtifactsResponse

TaskCreateParams.description: `task/create`: **only a human can start a long task** — there is no tool for it.

acceptance.description: How "done" is measured. Empty = the goal/judge decides, as before.

budget.description: Caps on the whole task's spend. Absent dimensions are uncapped.

codeChecks.description: Test-loop checks for a coding task. `after: "final"` becomes a `commandSucceeds` acceptance condition; `after: "edit"` runs after every `edit` / `apply_patch` and its output (4 KB at most) is appended to that tool's result.

cwd.description: The working directory this task owns. Absent = a new managed directory under home/workspaces.

goalCondition.description: Optional condition evaluated by the goal judge. Acceptance checks can also trigger additional rounds.

parentTaskId.description: The human-selected parent coding task whose worktree receives this child's checkpoint.

repo.description: A git repository (absolute path, chosen by the human). The task then runs in its own worktree on branch `jeeves/<task-id>`, which becomes its only working directory. Not combinable with `cwd`.

sessionId.description: Absent = the task belongs to no session: it can be created and inspected on its own.

tier.description: The model tier this task runs on (`fast` / `chat` / `reasoning`). Absent = decide per turn (auto mode) or use the active profile (fixed mode). A declared tier always wins — "the task picks the model" is the whole point of the tier.

title.description: What this task is, in the human's words — the card's first line.

TaskCreateParams.title: TaskCreateParams

TaskDeliveryView.description: The most recent terminal execution, including while a later revision is running.

TaskEventView.description: One entry of a task's timeline.
TaskEventView.title: TaskEventView

TaskEventsParams.description: `task/events`: every task event after `cursor` (absent = from the start), oldest first. The cursor is opaque to clients: pass back `nextCursor` to continue.

taskId.description: Narrow to one task. Absent = all tasks.

TaskEventsParams.title: TaskEventsParams

latestCursor.description: The newest cursor that exists (for the request's task filter). Lets a client tell "caught up" from "behind" without a second call.

nextCursor.description: Resume from here. Equals the request cursor when nothing is newer.

TaskGetParams.description: `task/get`: address one task by id (a session-less task has no other way in).
TaskGetParams.title: TaskGetParams

TaskGitCheckpointParams.description: Explicit human approval of the exact relative paths to commit in the task worktree.
TaskGitCheckpointParams.title: TaskGitCheckpointParams

TaskIntegrateParams.description: Integrate the exact reviewed head of a completed child into its pending parent worktree.
TaskIntegrateParams.title: TaskIntegrateParams

TaskListResponse.description: Newest first; `active` is the session's newest non-terminal task, when there is one.
TaskListResponse.title: TaskListResponse

TaskOperationsResponse.description: Human-only inspection of persisted tool operations and uncertainty.
TaskOperationsResponse.title: TaskOperationsResponse

TaskReconcileParams.description: Evidence records a human observation and never executes or resumes the operation.
TaskReconcileParams.title: TaskReconcileParams

TaskReviewCaptureParams.description: Attach two explicit commits from the completed task's repository.
TaskReviewCaptureParams.title: TaskReviewCaptureParams

TaskReviewFile.description: One file at the recorded delivery boundary.

TaskReviewView.description: Immutable file views for one delivered run.

TaskRunsResponse.description: `task/runs`: every attempt of one task, newest first.
TaskRunsResponse.title: TaskRunsResponse

TaskSignalParams.description: Authorized host input, correlated to an existing human-declared condition.
TaskSignalParams.title: TaskSignalParams

TaskStartParams.description: Start a pending task in its own durable execution context. Human-only.
TaskStartParams.title: TaskStartParams

TaskUpdatedNotification.description: A task changed state. The event bus folds it into a ping; the hub's `/api/tasks` shows the row.

sessionId.description: Absent for a task that belongs to no session.

TaskUpdatedNotification.title: TaskUpdatedNotification

TaskViewResponse.description: `task/view`: one session's current task (the card on screen).
TaskViewResponse.title: TaskViewResponse

TaskWaitParams.description: Human-only input declaration before a task starts.

expiresAt.description: Latest input arrival time; accepted data remains available after this deadline.

TaskWaitParams.title: TaskWaitParams

TaskWakeParams.description: `task/wake`: a channel message that may be the input a task is waiting for.

eventKey.description: Must match the waiting condition's event key (for example the chat id).

source.description: Must match the waiting condition's source (for example `lark`).

sourceKey.description: Unique per inbound message, `<channel>:<messageId>`. A repeat is skipped, never redelivered.

TaskWakeParams.title: TaskWakeParams

duplicate.description: This source key was seen before; nothing was delivered again.

taskId.description: The task that was woken (or had already been woken by this key).

woken.description: The message was delivered to a waiting task.

delta.description: A streaming text delta. Present only when `turn/start` passed `stream: true`.

TierRoute.description: One tier's entry in the routing table. `profile_id` absent = "follow the fallback chain" (`reasoning` → `chat` → active, `fast` → `chat` → active), i.e. what the router does anyway.

profileId.description: `null` is a real answer ("follow the chain"), so it is always on the wire — the panel distinguishes "not configured" from "field missing" by reading this, not by guessing.

TierRoute.title: TierRoute

TodoItemView.description: One row of the todo sheet. `status` is the wire form of `TodoStatus` (pending / in_progress / completed / cancelled) — a string, not an enum: the sheet is the model's vocabulary, the dashboard only paints it.

TodoListView.description: The whole sheet as the human sees it. `revision` is the board's monotonic version — the UI can tell "changed" from "refetched" with it.

output.description: The text the tool returned to the model. Failure details live here too — the turn is not aborted.

toolUseId.description: Same id as the matching `toolStarted`, so a client can settle the right row.

ToolDeltaNotification.description:
Live output from a tool that is **still running** (a long command's stdout).

Progress only: the `toolCompleted` that follows carries the real result, and that is what the model reads. A client that ignores this event loses liveness, not correctness.

chunk.description: A chunk of output, as it arrived. Chunk boundaries are not meaningful.

ToolDeltaNotification.title: ToolDeltaNotification

ToolEffect.description: Conservative effect used by both local tools and owner-declared connector manifests.
ToolEffect.title: ToolEffect

checkpointDigest.description: Per-turn snapshot for multi-turn ordinary-chat inspection.

origin.description: checkpoint / recovered_checkpoint; neither proves network transmission.

replayPolicy.description: Automatic replay policy; this journal grants no provider idempotency guarantees.

args.description: The model-supplied arguments; structure depends on the tool.

toolUseId.description: The id the model minted for this call — the same id its result comes back under. Clients key on it: several read-only calls can be in flight at once.

TurnAttachment.description: One image attached to a turn. `path` is **home-relative** (uploads land in `<home>/uploads/...`); the server reads the bytes and embeds them — the model never sees a path, it sees pixels. Only image files are accepted; other files keep the "path mentioned in text" route.

mediaType.description: Client-provided media type hint; the server trusts the file extension over this.

TurnCheckpointedNotification.description: A checkpoint has been written: this turn's working memory (model thoughts, tool results) is now in state.db — the loop can continue from here after a crash, finished tools are never re-run.

iterations.description: How many loop iterations are already done (a checkpoint lands at each tool-results boundary).

TurnCheckpointedNotification.title: TurnCheckpointedNotification

TurnFollowUpParams.description:
Queue one message to run **after** the turn that is currently running (0.16).

The difference from `turn/steer` is what the person means, not where the text goes: steer is "and also, while you are at it", follow-up is "when you are done". A follow-up becomes its own turn — its own rounds, budget and checkpoint — and runs even after this page is closed.
TurnFollowUpParams.title: TurnFollowUpParams

queued.description: Position in line: 1 = runs as soon as the current turn ends, 2 = after that one.

interrupted.description: false = this turn already finished; nothing was interrupted.

TurnListParams.description: Which turns are running. Absent `sessionId` = the whole home (the CLI's "what is happening").
TurnListParams.title: TurnListParams

TurnMeta.description: Telemetry for one turn. Persisted into chat_log.meta, so reopening an old session still shows which brain made which decision, not just the final reply.

goalRounds.description: How many rounds this goal has consumed up to this turn. 0 when no goal is set.

goalStatus.description: The goal loop's exit (`continuing` / `satisfied` / `impossible` / `round-limit` / `blocked`). `None` when no goal is set.

guardHits.description: How many times the loop guard fired this turn (0 = the model never got stuck repeating/alternating tool calls). Zero is normal; non-zero means part of this turn's budget went to spinning in place.

guardNote.description: What the guard told the model when it fired (a human-readable explanation; null otherwise).

interrupted.description: True when this turn was cut short by `turn/interrupt`. Older metas in the DB lack this field — `#[serde(default)]` lets them parse as before.

model.description: The model that actually answered this turn: the small model when the graph routed quick, recorded as-is.

retries.description: How many provider retries happened this turn (rate limits / transient faults). Zero is the norm.

routeReason.description: How this turn's model was chosen (routing, see route.rs): `auto:reasoning → ds-r1` or `fallback: …`. `None` in fixed mode and when the chosen one is already active — the footer stays quiet and only speaks when a choice/fallback actually happened.

usage.description: Token usage for this turn. The historical flaw of only reaching `turnCompleted` without being persisted is fixed: it now lands in chat_log with the meta, so past turns show their cost too.

TurnMeta.title: TurnMeta

TurnOperationsParams.description: Human-only inspection of stopped ordinary-chat operations; task operations use task/operations.
TurnOperationsParams.title: TurnOperationsParams

TurnResumedNotification.description: A checkpoint is being resumed: startup reconciliation found it unfinished and the loop continues from where it stood (finished tools are not re-run). The human said earlier "keep going until X" by starting the turn — resuming is not the model assigning itself work.

fromIterations.description: How many iterations the checkpoint had already completed.

reason.description: Why it is resuming (`reconcile: crash recovery`, …).

TurnResumedNotification.title: TurnResumedNotification

attachments.description: Images attached to this message, embedded as image content blocks. Requires a vision-capable provider; a missing or unreadable file fails the turn up front.

cwd.description: Working directory for this turn (per-turn override semantics): must be an existing absolute path (fail-closed admission); relative exec commands and relative read_file/list_dir paths resolve against it. Default = process cwd (old behavior).

requestId.description: Stable id of the message this turn answers (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, at most 120). A second `turn/start` with the same id in the same session replays the first turn's result instead of running again; the same id with a different message is refused.

stream.description: Whether to stream `textDelta` token by token. On for the dashboard, off for scripts.

tier.description: Pin this turn to a model tier (`fast` / `chat` / `reasoning`). Absent = let the server decide (task's declared tier, auto routing, or the active profile — in that order). Machine callers (task API, webhooks) say the tier; the model itself cannot.

TurnSteerParams.description:
Add one sentence to a turn that is already running (0.16).

Not `turn/start`: that one is refused while a turn runs (`SESSION_BUSY`), and for good reason — two turns on one session would interleave their writes. Steering is the supported way to say "and also" without cancelling work that has already happened.
TurnSteerParams.title: TurnSteerParams

queued.description: How many additions this turn has accepted so far, this one included — "queued: 1" reads as "it will be seen", "queued: 3" as "it is piling up behind two others".

TurnSteeredNotification.description: The human added a sentence to a running turn. Emitted to **every** client of the turn, so a second device sees the addition at the moment it happened instead of on the next reload.
TurnSteeredNotification.title: TurnSteeredNotification

TurnSuspendedNotification.description: A checkpoint is abandoned: the human interrupted the turn (or the session moved on) — it will NOT be auto-resumed. Suspended, not silently lost: the ledger says so.

reason.description: Why it was abandoned (`interrupted by user`, …).

TurnSuspendedNotification.title: TurnSuspendedNotification

TurnView.description: One turn that is running **right now** (in memory — a finished turn is simply gone).

startedAt.description: RFC 3339 with offset. The page computes "running for N minutes" from it, so the browser needs no second clock of its own.

TurnView.title: TurnView

UsageByModel.description: Response to `usage/summary`: per-model aggregates + totals. In hub mode this is per-user bookkeeping (one home and one state.db per user — the ledger is isolated by person by construction).
UsageByModel.title: UsageByModel

UsageSummaryParams.description: Params of `usage/summary`: an optional period, UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. `since` is inclusive, `until` exclusive; both absent = all time.
UsageSummaryParams.title: UsageSummaryParams
